transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I just feel like the future doesn’t hold much for me and that the meaningful part of my life is already over. My primary care doctor noticed this change in my outlook during my annual wellness visit and suggested I get a mental health evaluation.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful life event or major change, or have you been feeling this way most days for a long time? About how long has it been going on?

These feelings started creeping in after the initial excitement of my retirement from biomedical engineering began to wear off. It wasn't one sudden event, but this low, gray feeling has been going on pretty steadily for a little over three years now. It just feels like I've been marking time ever since.

During these past three years, have there been any periods lasting at least 2 months when your mood felt mostly back to normal, or has this low mood been there nearly all the time? Before this started, did you ever have separate episodes of depression that got better and then came back?

No, there haven't been any breaks; this low, gray feeling has been constant without any periods where I felt back to my normal self. Before this started after my retirement, I had never experienced any separate episodes of depression.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or acted more impulsively than normal? Even if it didn’t feel like a problem at the time, has anything like that ever happened?
No, I've never experienced anything like that at all. I have never had periods where I felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or needed less sleep, nor have I ever acted impulsively.

Over these three years, have you also had at least two of these most days: low energy, poor sleep or sleeping too much, low self-esteem, trouble concentrating or making decisions, poor appetite or overeating, or feeling especially hopeless?

Yes, I've definitely struggled with a couple of those, especially constant low energy and a deep sense of hopelessness. Even light tasks like running a few errands or spending a short time in my art studio completely wipe me out for the afternoon. I also have this persistent feeling that my life already peaked during my career, and now I'm just filling time until the clock runs out.

During these past 3 years, was there ever a period of at least 2 weeks when your depression became much worse than usual, with symptoms like losing interest in almost everything, major sleep or appetite changes, or strong guilt or thoughts of death? Or has it stayed at about the same low level the whole time?

It has stayed at about the same steady, low level the entire time. I haven't experienced any sudden, severe worsening, major changes in my sleep or appetite, or any thoughts of death. It's just been this persistent, unchanging "low, gray" feeling hanging over me for the past three years.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was [F34.1], and based on this conversation it remains the same. The interview supports a chronic depressed mood for over 3 years, present nearly continuously without remission periods of 2 months, with associated low energy and hopelessness. There is no history of elevated/expansive episodes, no prior discrete depressive episodes before onset, and no superimposed 2-week period of markedly worse symptoms, so alternatives such as episodic mood conditions are less likely. Sufficient evidence has been gathered for the current leading diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent depressed mood has been present nearly every day for over 3 years, with no symptom-free period of 2 months or more, accompanied by low energy and hopelessness. There is no history of manic/hypomanic symptoms, no prior major depressive episodes, and no superimposed major depressive episode during the course, supporting persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
